Trail Physics · Unit 6: Waves & Temperature · Module 17

Thermodynamics

Temperature, heat and thermal energy, heat transfer, the ideal gas law and the first and second laws.

Lesson coming

The question

Where does all your speed go when you brake down a long descent?

The physics

  • Temperature and temperature scales
  • Heat and thermal energy
  • Specific heat
  • Heat transfer
  • Ideal gas law
  • Internal energy
  • First and second laws

The math

  • Q = mcΔT
  • PV = nRT
  • ΔU = Q − W (Q = heat added to the system, W = work done by the system)

About the model: The Brake Heat Lab uses simplified energy-transfer assumptions (a hypothetical rotor and a chosen fraction of energy becoming heat) and states them.

Learning objectives

  • Tell temperature, heat and thermal energy apart, and convert temperature scales
  • Use Q = mcΔT
  • Estimate a brake’s temperature rise from kinetic energy, stating the assumptions
  • Use the ideal gas law for a tire
  • Apply the first law of thermodynamics with a stated sign convention
  • Explain the second law and why no engine is 100% efficient

Helps to know first: Energy and Gravitation.

The mountain biking connection

Braking turns kinetic energy into heat in the rotors and pads. Temperature also changes the pressure in tires and air shocks.

Learning activities
